title: Opportunistic Tool Shims and Client Snapshotting — PRD (WIP)
body:
Purpose
This doc proposes a pragmatic pattern for hosted API users who need robust streaming + tool-calling behavior in real-world, flaky-client and intermittent-network contexts. We combine two primary ideas: (1) opportunistic tool shims — transient, server-side adapters that satisfy tool contracts when a client cannot reach its own tool endpoints; and (2) client snapshotting — a lightweight resumable state snapshot serialized into the stream so thin clients (mobile, edge) can reconnect/resume without a full session replay.

Motivation / problem statements
- Mobile and embedded clients lose connectivity mid-stream frequently. Current partial-response/resume strategies require durable client state and/or long-lived server-side sessions (costly).
- Tool-calling contracts assume tool endpoints are reachable and idempotent. In practice third-party tools (webhooks, enterprise services) are behind corporate networks or require auth flows that clients can’t complete.
- SDK ergonomics are poor when developers must implement many failure modes (backpressure, partial parse, tool-handshake retries). We want the API/SDK to offer high-level, low-friction primitives.

Goals
- Provide a streaming surface that: a) enables resumable partial responses with compact snapshot payloads; b) exposes a first-class server-side opportunistic shim layer for tool resolution; c) keeps SDK wiring simple (1–2 primitives developers use).
- Minimize running cost: session snapshots should be bounded and garbage-collected; opportunistic shims should be ephemeral and only invoked when client negotiation fails.
- Preserve safety and security: shims run with explicit tenant-scoped, audited credentials; tool calls must log provenance and consent state.

Non-goals
- This is not an alternative to fully-managed Dedicated Private connectors for enterprise systems. Opportunistic shims are a best-effort fallback for public-tool-like integrations.
- Not addressing long-term offline batching of huge corpora (out of scope).

High-level flow (happy path + degraded path)
1) Client starts a streaming call with streaming=true, tools=[search,calendar,customWebhook], snapshot_policy={freq: 8k tokens, max_size: 32KB}.
2) Server streams partial tokens and attaches periodic Snap frames (binary or base64 blob) that encode enough state to reconstruct the session (prompt, current kv-cache pointer, outstanding tool calls and their causal ids).
3) Client loses connectivity after token N. On reconnect the client sends resume_token referencing last Snap frame id. Server reinstates ephemeral session (fast-path) and continues streaming from resumed KV state.

Degraded/tool-fallback scenario:
- If a tool call reaches a tool endpoint that is unreachable from the client, the SDK's default is to: attempt server-side shim resolution if tenant allows "opportunistic_shim: true". The shim will either proxy a best-effort HTTP request (with tenant-provided secrets stored in KMS) or attempt a synthetic response based on cached / indexed data (e.g., search index snapshot).
- The server marks the token stream with structured metadata: {frame_type: TOOL_RESULT, tool: calendar, resolution: shim/proxy/cached, provenance_id: P-12345}. This lets clients and audit pipelines reconcile results.

Structured streaming frames (suggested wire contract)
- TEXT_CHUNK: incremental text tokens
- SNAPSHOT_FRAME: base64(blob) + metadata {seq_id, kv_cursor, pending_tools: [ids], timestamp}
- TOOL_CALL_FRAME: {tool_id, call_id, input_schema}
- TOOL_RESULT_FRAME: {call_id, status, resolution: [direct|shim|cached|error], encoded_output}
- SESSION_END_FRAME: {final_metrics, snapshot_ref?}

Notes on encoding and size constraints
- Snapshot payloads should be gzip + base64 and constrained to <= 32KB by default. Policy configurable per-tenant.
- For very low-bandwidth clients SDKs should support SNAPSHOT_DIFF frames (LZ4 diff against last snapshot) to reduce bytes.

SDK ergonomics (developer-facing primitives)
- StreamingClient.start(StreamConfig cfg): returns StreamHandle with .on('text', cb), .on('tool', cb), .on('snapshot', cb), .resume(resume_token)
- Default SDK behavior should surface tool-call failures as ToolCall objects that have a .resolveWithShim() convenience method that toggles the opportunistic shim permission and retries via server.
- A single config flag (enableClientSnapshotting = true) should be the only opt-in needed for apps to get resume behavior; servers manage retention via tenant lifecycle and costs.

Security & Compliance
- Opportunistic shims require explicit tenant consent and should be disabled by default. For tenants that enable, we require a) tenant-provided allowlist, b) per-call consent header, c) audit log entry including original caller IP and shim execution environment id.
- Shim execution runs in a hardened micro-VM with restricted network egress. Secrets used by shims (for proxy) only accessible via short-lived KMS-derived tokens.

Metrics and observability
- New telemetry: snapshot_count_per_session, average_snapshot_size, resume_success_rate, shim_invocations, shim_success_rate, tool_mismatch_rate (direct vs shim vs cached), snapshot_restore_latency.
- Console additions: per-route snapshot retention view, per-tenant shim usage heatmap, trace linking of TOOL_CALL_FRAME -> shim execution logs.

Pricing / cost model implications
- Snapshots increase storage + egress; propose to: a) include snapshots in token-based billing as a small fixed surcharge per MB stored for <30d; b) offer a quota-free minimal snapshot budget for free-tier developer experience.

Developer stories / example flows
1) Chat app (mobile) — minimal changes: enableClientSnapshotting=true when creating StreamConfig. On reconnect, call StreamHandle.resume(token). Developer receives consistent partial stream without rehydrating full prompt.
2) Enterprise connector — tenant disallows shims; tool-call failures return TOOL_RESULT_FRAME with status=NEEDS_CLIENT_ACTION and client can present OAuth flow.
3) Hybrid — tenant allows shims for known public tools (e.g., weather API); shim used only when client unreachable, marked in stream metadata for audit.

Operational concerns and constraints
- Lifecycle GC: default snapshot retention 7 days; extendable via tenant plan. Snapshots older than retention are deleted and resume attempts fail with structured error RESUME_EXPIRED.
- Shim abuse: rate-limit shim invocations per-tenant and per-route. Track cost per shim call and surface to billing.

Backward compatibility and migration plan
- Existing streaming endpoints continue to work. New frames are additive; SDKs can ignore unknown frame types.
- Gradual rollout: (a) Beta: internal customers + 10 external customers; (b) Opt-in region flag; (c) General availability with telemetry-driven throttles.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Snapshot canonical format: should we standardize on a small protobuf vs JSON? Tradeoffs: protobuf smaller/typed; JSON easier for debugging.
- Should shims be able to transform outputs (normalize calendar TZs, redact PII) or only proxy? Draft principle: allow normalization with tenant-gated rules.
- Default snapshot size cap and diff algorithm selection for maximum cross-platform compatibility.

Next steps (owner: Aisha)
- Engineering spike (2 sprints) to prototype SNAPSHOT_FRAME encoding and resume handshake (owner: Mateo).
- Security review of shim runtime and KMS flows (owner: Claire).
- Draft SDK surface PR with two convenience methods: StreamClient.resume() and ToolCall.resolveWithShim() (owner: Benji).
- Customer-driven validation: identify 3 pilot customers (mobile chat, CRM connector, field app) — coordinate with solutions eng.

Appendix: example stream fragment (conceptual)
---BEGIN STREAM---
TEXT_CHUNK id=1: "Hi, I can look that up for you..."
SNAPSHOT_FRAME id=snap_1 meta={seq:1,kvcursor: 123,pending_tools:[tc_1]} payload=base64(gzip(...))
TOOL_CALL_FRAME call_id=tc_1 tool=calendar input={date_range}
TOOL_RESULT_FRAME call_id=tc_1 status=shim resolution=proxy encoded_output=base64(...) provenance=P-12345
TEXT_CHUNK id=2: "I found an opening on Friday at 3pm (calendar result)."
SESSION_END_FRAME final_metrics={tokens:342,elapsed_ms:1200}
---END STREAM---

Notes to reviewers
- Focus on the developer UX: is .resolveWithShim() intuitive? Would teams prefer explicit shim mode per-call?
- Security folks: what minimal audit fields are required for compliance?
- Billing: do snapshots belong in token billing or as storage surcharge?

(End of draft)
